chunks: Abān ibn ʿUthmān narrated that a man called Ibn Ziyād al-Ṭāʾī said:
I said to Abī ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام: “I had been a slave, and I married without the permission of my masters. Then Allah, Mighty and Majestic, set me free, so should I renew the marriage contract?”
So he said: “Did they know that you had married?”
I said: “Yes, they knew, remained silent, and did not say anything to me.”
So he said: “That is an acknowledgment from them. You remain upon your marriage.”

key_terms.أَعْتَقَنِي: granted me freedom or emancipated me

ai.seo_question: If a slave married without his master’s permission and was later freed, must the marriage contract be renewed?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling concerning the marriage of a slave who married without his masters’ permission and was later freed. Imam al-Ṣādiq عليه السلام states that if the masters knew of the marriage and remained silent, their silence counts as approval, and the original marriage remains valid without renewing the contract.

en.bab-ul-qaim-publications: Hadith.4549 - Aban ibn Uthman narrated that a man named Ibn Ziyad al-Ta'i said:
I said to Abu Abdillah (as): "I was a slave and got married without the permission of my masters. Then Allah (swt), the Mighty and Majestic, granted me freedom. Should I renew the marriage contract?"
Imam (as) said: "Were they aware that you had married?"
I said: "Yes, they knew and remained silent without objecting."
Imam (as) said: "Their silence is considered approval. You remain upon your original marriage contract."
